senses.gloss: श्वघ्निन् श्वघ्निन्. See col. 2.

श्वघ्निन्, ई, m. (according to some श्व is for
स्व, and the word is thought to mean ‘one who
destroys his own,’ others connect it with श्व-हन्),
Ved. a gamester, (Sāy. = देवन-शील.)

श्वङ्क् श्वङ्क् (also written स्वङ्क्), cl. 1.
A. श्वङ्कते, शश्वङ्के, श्वङ्कितुम्, to
go, move.

स्वङ्क् स्वङ्क् (= rt. श्वङ्क्), cl. 1. A. स्वङ्-
कते, &c., to go, move.

श्वङ्ग् श्वङ्ग् (also written श्रङ्ग्, स्वङ्ग्,
&c.; cf. rt. श्वङ्क्), cl. 1. P. श्वङ्गति,
श्वङ्गितुम्, to go, move.

स्वङ्ग् स्वङ्ग्, cl. 1. P. स्वङ्गति, &c., to
go, move (= rt. श्रङ्ग्, p. 1023).

श्वच् श्वच् or श्वञ्च् (= rts. शञ्च्, श्वज्),
cl. 1. A. श्वचते, श्वञ्चते, &c., (Ved.
form श्वञ्चयः, Ṛg-veda X. 138, 2; शश्वचै,
see s. v.), to go, move; to gape, open, be opened,
be split.

श्वज् श्वज् or श्वञ्ज् (= rts. श्वच्, शञ्च्), cl. 1.
A. श्वजते, श्वञ्जते, &c., to go, move.
श्वञ्च् श्वञ्च्. See above under rt. श्वच्.
स्वञ्च् स्व्-अञ्च्. See p. 1126, col. 2.

श्वठ् 1. श्वठ् (= rt. 2. शठ्), cl. 10. P.
श्वठयति, -यितुम्, to speak ill; (ac-
cording to some) to speak well or correctly; to be
accurate or true.

श्वठ् 2. श्वठ् or श्वण्ठ् (= rts. 3. शठ्,
स्वठ्, सठ्), cl. 10. P. श्वाठयति, श्वण्-
ठयति, &c., -यितुम्, to finish, accomplish, adorn;
to leave unfinished or unornamented; to go, move.

स्वठ् स्वठ् (= rt. 2. श्वठ्), cl. 10. P.
स्वाठयति, &c., to finish, &c.; to go.

श्वन् श्वन्, आ, m. (according to Uṇādi-s. I.
158. fr. rt. श्वि, perhaps fr. a participial base श्वन्त्;
Nom. sing. du. pl. श्वा, श्वानौ, श्वानस्; Acc. श्वा-
नम्, श्वानौ, शुनस्; Inst. शुना, श्वभ्याम्, &c.,
Gram. 155. a), a dog, hound, cur; (शुनी), f. a female
dog, bitch. श्वन् becomes श्वा for श्व in some com-
pounds, see below; [cf. Zend śpâ; Gr. κύ-ων,
κυνός (= शुनस्), ἁλ-κυών; Lat. can-i-s (for cvan-
i-s), catulus; Goth. hun-d-s; Lith. nom. szu§,
gen. szuns; Hib. nom. cu, gen. and pl. coin; Russ.
sobaka (for shaka); Pers. sag.]
—श्व-किष्किन्, ई,
इणी, इ, Ved. (according to some) having the tail of
a dog, (Sāy. connects किष्किन् with किष्कु, ‘a staff,
thunderbolt,’ Atharva-veda VIII. 6, 6.)
—श्व-क्री-
डिन्, ई, m. one who sports with dogs, a dog-feeder
or trainer, a breeder of sporting dogs.
—श्व-गण,
अस्, m. a pack or collection of dogs.
—श्वगणिक,
अस्, m. ‘one who has to do with packs of dogs,’ a
hunter; (अस्, ई), m. f. a dog-feeder; one who is drawn
by dogs.
—श्व-गणिन्, ई, इनी, इ, having packs of
hounds.
—श्व-ग्रह, अस्, m. ‘dog-seizure,’ epithet
of a particular disease or the deity presiding over
it.
—श्व-घ्नी, see under श्व-हन्.
—श्व-चाण्-
डाल, अम्, n. a dog and an outcast.
—श्व-चिल्ली, f.
a kind of pot-herb (= शुनक-चिल्ली).
—श्व-जा-
घनी, f. a dog's thigh, the haunch of a dog, (Manu
X. 108.)
—श्व-दंष्ट्रक, अस्, m. a kind of
plant (= गो-क्षुर).
—श्व-दंष्ट्रा, f. a dog's
tooth; a kind of plant (= गो-क्षुर).
—श्व-धूर्-
[]
त, अस्, m. ‘dog-rogue,’ a jackal.
—श्व-नर, अस्,
m. a dog-like fellow, low fellow, currish or snappish
fellow.
—श्व-निश, अम्, आ, n. f. ‘dog-night,’ a night
on which dogs bark and howl.
—श्व-पच्, क्, or श्व-
पच, अस्, आ, m. f. ‘dog-cooking,’ a man or woman
of a low and degraded caste, (see श्व-पाक); a
public executioner; a dog-feeder, dog-keeper; (ई), f.
a form of one of the Śaktis of Śiva.
—श्व-पद,
अम्, n. a dog's foot; a mark like a dog's foot to be
branded on the forehead of a thief.
—श्व-पाक, अस्,
m. ‘dog-cooking,’ a man of a degraded and outcast
tribe (described as son of an Ugra woman by a
Kṣatriya, and classed with the Caṇḍāla, q. v.; he
is required to live outside towns, to eat his food in
broken vessels, to wear the clothes of the dead, and
to be excluded from all intercourse with other tribes;
he can possess no other property than asses and dogs,
and his only office is to act as public executioner or
to carry out the bodies of those who die without
kindred); (ई), f. a woman of the above low or out-
cast tribe.
—श्व-फल, अम्, n. the lime or common
citron.
—श्व-फल्क, अस्, m., N. of the son of
Pṛśni (or according to others of Vṛṣṇi; he was
husband of Gāndinī, by whom he had a son named
Akrūra).
—श्व-भीरु, उस्, m. ‘dog-fearing,’ a jackal.
—श्व-भोजन, अस्, m. ‘having dogs for food,’ N.
of a Naraka.
—श्व-यातु, उस्, m., Ved. a demon in
the shape of a dog.
—श्व-यूथ्य, अम्, n. a number or
pack of dogs.
—श्व-रूप-धारिन्, ई, इणी, इ, wearing
or having the form of a dog.
—१. श्व-वत्, आन्, m.
possessing or keeping a dog, a dog-feeder, dog-
trainer.
—२. श्व-वत्, ind. like a dog, cur-like.
—श्व-वृत्ति, इस्, f. the life of a dog; condition of
a dog; service, servitude (which a Brāhman ought
not to engage in).
—श्व-व्याघ्र, अस्, m. a beast
of prey, a tiger; the hunting leopard or Chīta.
—श्व-सुत, अस्, m. the plant Conyza Aspera.
—श्व-
स्पृष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, touched by a dog, defiled.
—श्व-हत, अस्, आ, अम्, killed by a dog, killed by
dogs.
—श्व-हन्, आ, घ्नी, अ, Ved. one who kills
with dogs; (आ), m. a hunter; (घ्नी), f. the wife
of a hunter.
—श्वा-कर्ण, अस्, m. a dog's ear.
—श्वा-दन्त, अस्, m. (श्वा for श्व), a dog's tooth.
—श्वा-पद, अस्, m. a beast of prey, wild beast; a
tiger; (अस्, ई, अम्), relating or belonging to a wild
beast, ferocious, savage, (in this sense properly an
adj. fr. श्वा-पद, and therefore to be written
without a hyphen.)
—श्वापद-सेवित, अस्, आ, अम्,
frequented or infested by wild beasts.
—श्वापदा-
चरित (˚द-आच्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, overrun or infested by
wild beasts.
—श्वापदानुसरण (˚द-अन्˚), अम्,
n. the pursuit or chase after a wild animal.
—श्वा-
पुच्छ, अस्, अम्, m. n. a dog's tail.
—श्वाविच्-
छरण, अम्, n. (i. e. श्वा-विध्, see below, + शर-
ण), the lair or resting-place of a porcupine, (a
porcupine's hole has always two or more entrances.)
—श्वा-विध्, त्, m. (श्वा for श्व), a porcupine, hedge-
hog.
—श्वाश्व (श्व-अश्˚), अस्, m. ‘having a dog
for a horse,’ epithet of Bhairava (or Śiva in a ter-
rific form, sometimes represented as mounted on
a dog).

स्वन् स्वन्, cl. 1. P. स्वनति, सस्वान (3rd
pl. सस्वनुस् or स्वेनुस्), स्वनिष्यति,
अस्वनीत् or अस्वानीत्, स्वनितुम्, to sound, make a
noise; to sing: Caus. स्वनयति, -यितुम्, Aor. असि-
स्वनत्, to cause to sound, make to resound; to
sound; to adorn (in this sense also स्वानयति, &c.):
Desid. सिस्वनिषति: Intens. संस्वन्यते, सं-
स्वन्ति; [cf. Lat. son-o; Lith. zwanu, ‘to sound;’
Hib. sian, ‘a voice, sound.’]
श्व at the end of comps. = श्वन् above.

स्व 1. स्व, अस्, आ, अम्, own, one's own, my
own, thy own, his own, our own, &c. (according
to the context; and in these senses frequently used
at the beginning of comps.; when declined, स्व is
generally treated as a pronominal, and follows सर्व,
e. g. स्वस्मै dat. c. sing., स्वस्मात् abl. c. sing.,
स्वस्मिन् loc. c. sing., but in abl. loc. sing. Nom.
pl. it optionally follows शिव, e. g. तं स्वयम्-
भूः स्वाद् आस्याद् असृजत्, him, the self-existent,
created from his own mouth, Manu I. 94; when,
however, स्व is used as a substantive, meaning
‘kinsman’ and ‘property,’ it cannot be declined as
a pronominal, but must necessarily follow the de-
clension of शिव, e. g. स्वाः, one's own relations,
प्रभूताः स्वाः, great riches), innate, native, natural,
inherent, proper, peculiar, appropriate; belonging to
one's own family or tribe; (अस्), m. self, one's own
self, self-identity; the soul; N. of Viṣṇu; a kins-
man, relative, relation, (Manu II. 109); (अस्, अम्),
m. n. property, wealth, riches; (in algebra) plus or
affirmative quantity; [cf. Zend hva, qa: Gr. ἑ, ϝε
(for αϝε), σφέ (οὖ, οἴ, ἕ), ἑ-ό-ς, ὅ-ς, σφ-ό-ς, ἴ-διο-ς:
Lat. se, suu-s: Goth. si-k, ‘self;’ sves, ‘own;’
svesa, ‘property;’ sei-na (for svei-na), sve, svi in
svi-kunths, ‘manifest:’ Old Germ. suâs, ‘own:’
Angl. Sax. sin, swa: Lith. saw, sawa-s, sawa:
Slav. sebje, sebe, svoi, svaja, svœ, svo-bodi, ‘free;’
svo-boda, ‘liberty.’]
—स्व-कम्पन, अस्, m. ‘self-
moving,’ air, wind.
—स्व-कर्म-कृत्, त्, m. doing
one's own business, an independent workman.
—स्व-
कर्मन्, अ, n. one's own work, own business, own
duty, peculiar or proper business.
—स्व-कर्म-
वश, अस्, आ, अम्, subject to (the consequences of)
one's own acts.
—स्व-कर्म-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्,
minding one's own business or duty.
—स्व-कामिन्,
ई, इनी, इ, self-loving, selfish.
—स्व-कार्य, अम्, n.
one's own business or duty or function.
—स्व-कार्य-
सह, अस्, आ, अम्, able to do one's duty or effect
one's own business.
—स्व-कुटुम्ब, अम्, n. one's
own household.
—स्व-कुल, अम्, n. one's own
family or race.
—स्व-कुल-क्षय, अस्, m. ‘destroy-
ing its own family,’ a fish.
—स्व-कृत, अस्, आ, अम्,
self-performed, done or made by one's self.
—स्व-
क्षत्र, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. possessing innate strength,
self-powerful, innately strong.
—स्व-गत, अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘gone to one's self,’ passing in one's own mind,
spoken to one's self, apart, aside; (अम्), n. to one's
self, aside (in theatrical language).
—स्व-गर्भ,
अस्, m. own womb; own embryo.
—स्व-गुण-तस्,
ind. from personal merit.
—स्व-गुण-प्रकाशक,
अस्, इका, अम्, proclaiming one's own merits, boast-
ful.
—स्व-गुप्त, अस्, आ, अम्, self-defended, self-
[]
preserved; (आ), f. cowach; the sensitive plant (=
लज्जालु).
—स्व-गूर्त, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. sponta-
neously striving, (Sāy. = स्वयम्-उद्यत, Ṛg-veda
VI. 68, 4); self-flowing, spontaneously going (said
of rivers; Sāy. = स्वयम् एव गामिन्, Ṛg-veda I.
140, 13).
—स्व-गृह, अम्, n. one's own house;
(अस्), m. a kind of bird, Loxia Philippensis.
—स्व-
ग्राम, अस्, m. one's own village.
—स्व-चरण-
पर्षद्, त्, f. a college or community of members
of one's own Caraṇa or sect.
—स्व-च्छन्द, अस्, m.
one's own will, own choice, own fancy; independ-
ence; (अस्, आ, अम्), self-willed, independent, un-
controlled; spontaneous; uncultivated, wild; (अम्),
ind. according to one's own will or choice or fancy,
voluntarily, spontaneously, independently.
—स्व-
च्छन्दक, अस्, आ, अम्, = स्व-च्छन्द above.
—स्वच्छन्द-चारिणी, f. ‘going about at will,’ a
harlot.
—स्वच्छन्द-तस्, ind. voluntarily.
—स्वच्-
छन्द-भैरव, N. of a work.
—स्वच्छन्द-
शाक्तागम (˚त-आग्˚) and स्वच्छन्द-सङ्ग्रह,
अस्, m., N. of two works.
—स्व-ज, अस्, आ, अम्,
self-produced, self-born, produced in or by one's
self; (अस्), m. a son; sweat, perspiration; (आ), f.
a daughter; (अम्), n. blood.
—स्व-जन, अस्, m.
one's own people, own kindred, own family or
household; a kinsman, connection.
—स्वजनाय,
Nom. A. स्वजनायते, -यितुम्, to become a relation.
—स्व-जनावृत (˚न-आव्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, surrounded
or accompanied by one's own people.
—स्व-जाति,
इस्, f. own cast or tribe, own kind or species.
—स्व-
जातीय or स्व-जात्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to one's
own tribe or species.
—स्व-ज्ञाति, इस्, f. one's own
kindred or kin; (इस्), m. a kinsman.
—स्वतः-
प्रमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, self-proved, self-evident.
—स्वतः-सिद्ध, अस्, आ, अम्, self-accomplished;
self-proved, self-demonstrated.
—स्व-तन्त्र, अस्, आ,
अम्, self-dependent, self-reliant, independent, free,
self-willed, unrestrained, uncontrolled; no longer
subject to parents, of age, full grown; (अम्), n., N.
of a mystical work.
—स्वतन्त्र-ता, f. self-depend-
ence, self-reliance, independence; wilfulness.
—स्व-
तन्त्र-वृत्ति, इस्, f. acting self-reliantly, independent
action.
—स्वतन्त्र-सार, अस्, m., N. of a work.
—स्व-तवस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. having power in
one's self, having innate or peculiar power, very
strong or powerful (said of the Maruts); having
wealth in one's self, (Sāy. स्व-तवान्, nom. c.
masc. = धन-वान्, Ṛg-veda IV. 2, 6; cf. Pāṇini
VIII. 3, 11, VII. 1, 83); firmly rooted (said of a
mountain).
—स्व-तस्, ind. by one's self, in one's
self, of one's self (applicable to any person, e. g.
by himself, in himself, &c., by itself, in itself, of
itself, &c.); own, peculiar.
—स्वतस्-सिद्ध, see
स्वतः-सिद्ध.
—स्व-ता, f. = स्व-त्व, q. v.
—स्व-
त्र, अस्, आ, अम्, self-preserving; (अस्), m. a blind
man.
—स्व-त्व, अम्, n. ‘selfness,’ self-existence,
independent being or condition; the state of relation
to one's self; own right or property, ownership,
proprietorship, proprietary right.
—स्वत्व-निवृत्ति,
इस्, f. cessation or loss of proprietary right.
—स्वत्व-
बोधन, अम्, n. declaration or proof of ownership.
—स्वत्व-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having proprietary right;
(आन्), m. an owner.
—स्वत्व-व्यभिचारि-त्व, अम्,
n. uncertainty of ownership.
—स्वत्व-व्यभिचारिन्,
ई, इणी, इ, departing or deviating from ownership.
—स्वत्व-हानि, इस्, f. loss of proprietary right, for-
feiture of title.
—स्वत्व-हेतु, उस्, m. ground or
cause of proprietary right.
—स्वत्वाभाव (˚व-
अभ्˚), अस्, m. non-existence of proprietary right.
—स्वत्वावगम (˚व-अव्˚), अस्, m. determination
or ascertainment of ownership.
—स्वत्वास्पद (˚व-
आस्˚), अम्, n. site of ownership, that in which any
one has proprietorship.
—स्वत्वास्पदी-भूत, अस्, आ,
अम्, become the subject of proprietary right.
—स्व-
त्वोत्पत्ति (˚व-उत्˚), इस्, f. the arising of proprietary
right, origin of ownership.
—स्व-दार, अस्, m. one's
own wife.
—स्वदार-निरत, अस्, आ, अम्, attached
to one's wife, uxorious.
—स्व-दुहितृ, ता, f. one's
own daughter.
—स्व-देश, अस्, m. own country,
native country, home; one's own place, proper
place.
—स्वदेश-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, born in one's
[]
country, a fellow-countryman, compatriot.
—स्व-
देश-परिधि, इस्, m. circumference of a circle of
longitude in any place that has latitude.
—स्वदेश-
मध्य-परिधि, इस्, m. circumference of the ter-
restrial equator.
—स्व-देह-दान, अम्, n. the gift
of one's own body.
—स्व-धर्म, अस्, अम्, m. n.
own right, own duty, peculiar duty or occupation,
the duties of one's own class or caste (as defined
in Manu I. 88 — 91), peculiar property, peculiarity.
—स्वधर्म-च्युत, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived of one's
rights, fallen from or neglecting one's duty.
—स्व-
धर्म-त्याग, अस्, m. dereliction or neglect of
one's own duty; abandoning one's religion, apostasy.
—स्वधर्म-स्खलन, अम्, n. falling from or
neglect of one's own duty.
—स्वधर्म-स्थ, अस्, आ,
अम्, abiding in one's peculiar duty.
—स्वधर्मा-
चरण (˚म-आच्˚), अम्, n. the act of practising one's
own duties.
—स्वधर्मानपग (˚म-अन्˚), अस्,
आ, अम्, not swerving from one's duties.
—स्वधर्-
मार्थ-विनिश्चय, अस्, m. the knowing or ascer-
taining one's duty and interests.
—स्व-धा, see s.v.
—स्व-नगर, अम्, n. one's own town, native city.
—स्व-नामन्, अ, n. one's own name.
—स्वना-
माङ्क (˚म-अङ्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, marked with one's
own name, called after one's own name.
—स्व-नाश,
अस्, m. self-destruction.
—स्व-पक्ष, अस्, m. one's
own side, own party; ‘being on one's own side,’ a
friend.

यानि); manner, habit, custom, usage, (अनु स्वधाम्,
according to one's wont or custom, as usual; ac-
cording to one's own determination, according to

offering due to each god; the food or oblation
offered to the Pitṛs or spirits of deceased ancestors

dha or funeral ceremony itself; the Food or Obla-

II. 7; = उदक, Naigh. I. 12); (स्वधा), ind. an

genitors [cf. स्वाहा, श्रौषट्, वौषट्, वषट्],

स्वर, अस्, m. sound, noise; voice; tone, tune,
music, a primary musical sound, note of the musical
scale or gamut (of which there are seven, commonly
thus arranged, 1. निषाद, 2. ऋषभ, 3. गान्-
धार, 4. षड्ज, 5. मध्यम, 6. धैवत,
7. पञ्चम; these notes are described as resem-
bling respectively the notes of an elephant, bull, goat,
peacock, curlew or heron, horse, and Koil; they are
designated by their initial letters or syllables thus,
नि, ऋ, ग, ष, म, ध, प, and the order is some-
times changed, षड्ज being placed first, पञ्चम
fifth, and निषाद last); a symbolical expression for
the number seven; a vowel (either ह्रस्व short,
दीर्घ long, or प्लुत prolated); an accent, tone (of
which there are three, viz. उदात्त, अनुदात्त, and
स्वरित, see below); air breathed through the nostrils,
nasal sound; snoring; (आ), f., N. of the chief wife of
Brahmā (Gāyatrī being the other).
—स्वर-गता-
ध्यय (˚त-अध्˚), अस्, m., N. of the first book of
the Saṅgīta-darpaṇa; of the first book of the Saṅ-
gīta-ratnākara.

scale, gamut.

lowed by a sibilant or other consonant without the
intervention of a vowel (e. g. वर्ष pronounced
वरिष).
—स्वर-भङ्ग, अस्, m. interruption or
indistinctness of utterance, broken articulation, crack-
ing of the voice, hoarseness, fluttering of the voice,
any defect in speaking (caused by emotion or morbid
affections of the chest).

very few.

selves spontaneously to the chariot.

षण), the peculiar characteristics or natural dis-

स्वाहा स्वाहा (probably for स्व्-आधा, i. e. 5.

lation personified (as a wife of Agni and goddess

sented also as a wife of the Rudra Paśu-pati; cf. स्व-
धा); a female Bauddha divinity; in Naigh. I. 11.
स्वाहा is enumerated among the वाङ्-नामानि;
(ind.) an exclamation used in making oblations to
the gods (often used like ‘Hail!’ and governing a
dat. case, e. g. अग्नये or सोमाय स्वाहा; cf. स्व्-अस्ति).
—स्वाहा-कार, अस्, m. utterance of the term Svāhā;
the formula Svāhā (uttered at the end of the Yājyā
verses).
—स्वाहा-कृति, इस्, f., Ved. an oblation made
with the Svāhā-kāra, (Ṛg-veda X. 110, 11. is ad-
dressed to the Svāhā-kṛtis.)
—स्वाहा-पति, इस्, m.
‘lord of the Svāhā,’ Agni.
—स्वाहा-प्रिय, अस्, m.
‘fond of the Svāhā,’ Agni.
—स्वाहा-भुज्, क्, m.
‘eating the Svāhā,’ a deity.

स्वरण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. illustrious, celebrated,
(Sāy. = देवेषु प्रकाशन-वत्, Ṛg-veda I. 18, 1.)

स्वरित, अस्, आ, अम्, sounded; sounded as a note,
pitched; articulated; accented; having the mixed
or circumflex accent, circumflexed; (अस्), m. the third
or mixed tone between high and low, which is
thought to correspond with the circumflex accent,
(the other two tones being called Ud-ātta and An-
[]
udātta, q.q. v.v.; the Ud-ātta sound of a vowel is
said to result from the employing the upper half of
the organs of utterance, and the An-udātta from em-
ploying the lower half, while the Svarita represents
a sustained mixed intonation neither high nor low,
which is well illustrated by the expression तिर्यग्-
गमन, i. e. a horizontal or wavy movement of
the hand as distinguished from a direct upward and
downward motion; Pāṇini, however, applies the
term अन्-उदात्त, ‘non-elevated,’ to the neutral accent-
less tone, and uses the term सन्न-तर or अन्-
उदात्त-तर for ‘the very or proper An-udātta,’ i. e.
the true grave accent which precedes the Udātta;
in I. 2, 31. he calls the Svarita सम्-आहार, i. e. ‘a
combination’ of the elevated and non-elevated tones;
the Svarita accent is denoted in the Ṛg-veda by a
small upright stroke above the syllable, the Anudātta-
tara by a horizontal mark underneath, and the Udātta
is left unmarked; but the Svarita mark may denote
either a dependent or an independent Svarita, i. e.
one produced by an Udātta immediately preceding
or a real Svarita belonging to the word itself, and
commonly produced by the suppression of an Udātta
syllable; again, as a word is supposed to have only
one real accent, so words which have real Svaritas
of their own do not have Udātta accents; they are
called आदि-स्वरित, मध्य-स्वरित, अन्त-स्वरित,
according as they have Svaritas on the first, middle,
or last syllable; it must also be borne in mind that
when a dependent Svarita is immediately followed
by an Udātta, the Svarita becomes a kind of Anudātta-
tara, and is so marked, see ताथाभाव्य; there were,
doubtless, different kinds of Svarita pronunciation.)
—स्वरित-त्व, अम्, n. the state of having the Svarita
accent.
—स्वरितोपध (˚त-उप्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, pre-
ceded by the Svarita; having the penultimate marked
with the Svarita.

स्वरितृ, ता, त्री, तृ, one who sings, a singer
(Ved.); one who pains or afflicts, a painer (= उप-
तापयितृ, but perhaps to be connected with rt. स्वॄ).
स्वरुस्, उस्, m. a thunderbolt (= स्वरु above).

स्वर्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being accented with the
Svarita, circumflexed.
